summary: M3 dual-write backend verification: 42/42 tests pass — 13 new HTTP-layer E2E (test_m3_e2e_dualwrite.py) + 14 M3 unit (test_m3_dualwrite.py) + 15 M2 regression baseline (test_m2_backfill.py). Live parity report against the preview DB returns ok=True across all 17 invariants (I1–I8). V1 contract verified intact: citizen register/OTP login responses still carry id/role/tenant_id/household_id/issue_code/status AND now additionally carry person_id + origin_membership_id (additive, non-breaking). Issue full lifecycle (create→assign→In Progress→Resolved→feedback) returns V1 shape and emits the corresponding V2 timeline events. Visit/Notification/DevWork creation by PA/admin returns V1 shape and the parity stamping holds. Interaction creation by PA against citizen subject works and stamps person_id of the subject. Profile update via PUT /api/persons/{id} accepts allowed fields and mirrors. Parity endpoint correctly returns 403 for tenant admin + PA and 200 for super_admin; backfill is idempotent.

minor.issue: Response body does not include person_id / origin_membership_id even though dual-write stamps them in V2. Citizens' /auth/citizen/register response correctly includes both via the post-write update. For staff the V1 row itself isn't updated post-dualwrite (mapping lives in _v2_user_to_person collection). Not a contract regression (additive only) but inconsistent with the citizen flow — consider stamping for parity of UX/observability.

Allowed update fields do not include core identity fields (name/dob/gender/email/mobile) — only profile metadata (occupation, notes, profile_photo, status, etc). v2_dualwrite.sync_person_profile_update declares 'name/dob/gender/email' as allowed but the V1 endpoint will never let them through, so that branch is effectively dead code from the HTTP layer.

action_items: (Optional, minor) After dual-write of a staff user in POST /api/admin/staff, write back person_id (and origin_membership_id) onto the V1 users row for symmetry with the citizen register flow — frontend can then read it directly without an extra mapping fetch.

(Optional, minor) Either expand the PUT /api/persons/{id} allowed-fields set to include name/dob/gender/email so sync_person_profile_update's full projection is reachable, or trim those keys from the helper to make the contract explicit.

(Optional) Add a dedicated assertion in the parity report for the inverse: 'every staff Person has staff-scope membership AND current_organisation_id IS NULL' — currently I3 only checks citizens; staff invariants are only implicitly covered by I4/I7.
critical_code_review_comments: v2_dualwrite.py: dualwrite helpers correctly swallow exceptions and emit logger.exception — V1 durability is preserved. Idempotency proven via test_ensure_person_idempotent + test_parity_backfill_idempotent.

server.py citizen_register (557-625): after ensure_person_for_user it correctly writes person_id + origin_membership_id back onto the users row inside a try/except that never bubbles up — good pattern.

server.py create_staff (~715): returns u.model_dump() built BEFORE the dual-write, so staff V1 response lacks person_id. Either re-fetch after dual-write or move the response build below the try-block (minor).
server.py update_status uses query parameter style in some legacy callers but the route signature requires JSON body (IssueUpdateStatus). Verified body-style is the supported contract. No regression.

parity_report aggregates over potentially large collections without limits (I4/I5 iterate persons & timeline_events). For larger tenants this may become slow — consider adding an index on persons.id (unique) and person_timeline_events.person_id, and chunked scanning.
Per Rule: MongoDB _id excluded properly via projections in all read paths (server.py uses {'_id': 0} consistently).
All dual-write side-effects mark rows with _dualwrite_marker='dualwrite_m3', giving the nightly parity asserter a way to attribute V2 rows back to their write — good observability hook.

rca of the issue: No bug RCA needed — all assertions passed after correcting only test-script payload shapes to match server contract: (a) /api/auth/citizen/register requires region_type; (b) /api/issues/{id}/assign expects {assigned_to} not {worker_id}; (c) /api/issues/{id}/status requires JSON body {status}; (d) /api/issues/{id}/feedback requires {rating, comment, verified}; (e) PUT /api/persons/{id} is staff-only and only accepts a fixed allowed-fields set (occupation/notes/etc.). These are stable V1 contracts and were already documented in the older regression suite; the test fixes were applied to the script, not the backend.
